findings.title: `source_bar_stamping` accepts plain strings and fails with `TypeError` on unhashable input
findings.description:
`Market.__post_init__` checks `self.source_bar_stamping not in SOURCE_BAR_STAMPINGS`. `TimeMeaning` is a `StrEnum` (`timestamps.py:37`), and a `StrEnum` member hashes and compares equal to its string value. So the plain string `"period_start"` passes the membership test and is stored as a `str`, not a `TimeMeaning`.

The other enum fields (`continuity_kind`, `session_mode`, `adjustment_bases`) go through `_require_instance`. The tests cover that gap for `continuity_kind` (`"adjusted"` is rejected) but not for `source_bar_stamping`. The two canonicalize to the same bytes, so the hash does not change. Any caller that uses `is TimeMeaning.PERIOD_START`, or a `match` on the member, would behave differently for a value that passed validation.

An unhashable value such as a list also raises a raw `TypeError` from the `in` check, not `InvalidMarketError`. Add `_require_instance(self.source_bar_stamping, TimeMeaning, ...)` before the membership check. Add test rows for `"period_start"` and for an unhashable value.

findings.title: `_require_instance` is duplicated across `markets.py` and `instruments.py`
findings.description: The two helpers have the same body and differ only in the exception class they raise (`InvalidMarketError` and `InvalidInstrumentError`). The project rules say not to duplicate logic. A single helper that takes the error type, or a shared private validation module, would fix this. Both modules must still avoid importing `calendars` and `canonical`, so a small `_validation` module would fit the import-boundary test. The `_require_nonempty_str` and `_require_positive_decimal` checks have the same shape and could move there too.

findings.title: Declared field types do not match what the constructor accepts
findings.description: `session_calendars` is annotated `tuple[SessionCalendarRef, ...]` and `adjustment_bases` as `frozenset[AdjustmentBasis]`. The docstring says both accept any iterable, and the tests pass lists, generators and sets. Under the strict pyright the project requires, a typed caller passing a list gets an error. The tests avoid this by building the fields as `dict[str, Any]`, which hides the mismatch. Either annotate the constructor inputs honestly (for example with `InitVar` or a factory classmethod), or drop the "any iterable" claim and require a tuple and frozenset. A non-iterable value, such as a single `SessionCalendarRef`, gives a raw `TypeError` from `tuple(refs)` instead of `InvalidMarketError`.

findings.title: Timezone name is not checked against any zone database
findings.description: `timezone_name` is only checked for being a non-empty `str`. The module docstring says it is opaque (D2), so this is by design. A typo such as `"America/New_Yrok"` therefore only fails when something resolves it later. If trading-data is meant to be the validating authority, a one-line note in the docstring would make that explicit.

findings.title: Fixture modules ship inside the `src` package
findings.description: The new fixture markets and instruments follow the existing `fixtures/calendars.py` pattern. Their `fixture-` prefixes and docstrings mark them as non-served data, and the module-level construction validates them at import time. No action is needed. This is only a reminder that production imports are not blocked from reaching them.

findings.title: Golden coverage for markets and instruments is hash-only
findings.description: The market and instrument rows pin only the hash, with `None` for the bytes. The comment says the hashes were computed independently from 101's rules, which I could not verify. The "order does not change bytes" test and the one-fact-changes-the-hash tests cover the main risks. A single byte-level golden row for one instrument would also pin the embedded-market layout (`$set` ordering and session-ref ordering) in readable form.

findings.title: Contract-terms validation and error taxonomy
findings.description: `ContractTerms` uses exact-type checks (`type(value) is Decimal`), so `bool`, `float` and `int` are rejected. It checks `is_finite()` before comparing to zero, which keeps signaling NaN from raising. The currency check uses `fullmatch`, so `"USD\n"` fails, and the tests cover that case. The four new errors all subclass `CoreModelError`. The `UNKNOWN` handling goes through `is_known` and never takes a truth test.

findings.title: Test structure and uniformity
findings.description: One parameterized test body runs every fixture through calendar resolution, `period_end` and terms with no branching on market, which enforces the "a market is a market" rule. The tests are parameterized and independent. The import-boundary test is extended to the new modules, and the new `FIXTURE_CALENDARS` mapping is read-only and keyed by each calendar's own id, with tests for both.

structured_findings.summary: `source_bar_stamping` accepts plain strings and fails with `TypeError` on unhashable input
Declared field types do not match what the constructor accepts
Timezone name is not checked against any zone database
Fixture modules ship inside the `src` package
Golden coverage for markets and instruments is hash-only
